hero.title: HookLens labels the hooks that keep you scrolling
hero.description:
Upload an app screenshot, mark addictive UI regions, and get a readable Addiction Report.
Not Screen Time. Not a blocker. A name tag on the trap.

announcement.title: Mark hooks → get a shareable report

introduce.title: See the trap on the screen
introduce.label: Product
introduce.description: HookLens turns vague “this app is addictive” into labeled regions you can show a friend in under two minutes.

items.title: Screenshot in
items.description: Upload your own capture or pick a sample — including a Looply feed screenshot.

items.title: Boxes on the hooks
items.description: Drag rectangles onto infinite scroll, badges, related rails, autoplay — and write why it pulls you back.

items.title: Report out
items.description: Generate a summary plus findings list you can reopen and share on /report.

benefits.title: Why HookLens
benefits.label: Benefits
benefits.description: Built for a public-education demo, not another productivity lock.

items.title: Name the mechanism
items.description: Shared dictionary with Patterns: infinite scroll, unread badges, related rabbit holes, autoplay.

items.title: Works in the browser
items.description: No extension install for the demo path — open Analyze and start marking.

items.title: Point to cleaner options
items.description: After the report, browse Apps that aim to drop the worst hooks.

usage.title: Three steps
usage.description: The demo path from blank page to “oh — that’s what got me.”

items.title: 1. Pick a screenshot
items.description: Use the Looply sample or upload a PNG/JPG from any app.

items.title: 2. Annotate hooks
items.description: Draw boxes, choose a hook type, add a one-line note and severity.

items.title: 3. Generate Report
items.description: Open the read-only report with summary, marked image, and next links.

items.question: Is this a Screen Time / blocker app?
items.answer: No. HookLens labels addictive design on screenshots so people can see the mechanism — it does not lock your phone.

items.question: Do I need a browser extension?
items.answer: Not for this demo. The core path is the web Analyze tool. An extension may come later.

items.question: Where is my report stored?
items.answer: In this browser’s local storage for the demo. Cross-device sharing is a later upgrade.

items.question: Are the sample images real apps?
items.answer: No — samples include a Looply feed capture and simple wireframes so you can practice without trademark issues.
